key.label: Watch for easing
key.text: New supply closes grid capacity shortfalls; gas-turbine lead times shorten; Texas connections resume and approvals rise.

calls.depends: New supply arrives around 2030: turbine expansion, the PJM Interconnection backstop auction and new 765 kilovolt lines in Texas. Near-term data point the other way, so the rating reverts to Severe if these signposts do not turn.

sps.name: Capacity auctions
sps.track: PJM Interconnection's main capacity auction: shortfall against the reliability requirement, procured against target reserve margin, new generation cleared, and clearing price against the cap.
sps.trigger: Positive if the 2029/30 shortfall is below 6,831 megawatts, the margin rises from 14.7% towards 20%, more new generation clears, and uncapped prices come back towards the cap.
sps.latest: Shortfall 6,831 megawatts; reserve margin 14.7%
sps.sources: PJM auction results and planning parameters; Monitoring Analytics (independent market monitor); Utility Dive

sps.name: Emergency procurement
sps.track: New generation PJM contracts in its one-off backstop auction, against a target of about 6.8 gigawatts.
sps.trigger: Positive if contracted capacity approaches the target on schedule.
sps.latest: Auction suspended by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)
sps.next: Bid opening proposed 1 Mar; target reset 28 Apr 2027
sps.sources: FERC eLibrary docket alerts; PJM news releases and board materials

sps.name: Turbine supply
sps.track: GE Vernova gas turbine backlog plus slot reservations against quarterly shipments, and the earliest delivery year on sale.
sps.trigger: Positive if quarterly additions fall below shipments, so the backlog stops rising, and pre-2030 delivery slots reappear.
sps.latest: Gas equipment backlog plus slot reservations 122 gigawatts, up from 116 a quarter earlier. In the quarter: 11 gigawatts signed, 5 shipped.
sps.sources: US Securities and Exchange Commission filings; GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries results; US Energy Information Administration monthly generator file

history.measure: Gas equipment backlog plus slot reservations

sps.name: Texas connections
sps.track: Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) queue of large loads of 75 megawatts or more, capacity approved to energise, and the status of the pause.
sps.trigger: Positive if approvals grow faster than about 2 gigawatts a year, the approved share rises and the queue stops growing.
sps.latest: About 2% of the queue approved; connections paused
sps.next: Statewide audit report 10 Dec 2026; new governor 19 Jan 2027
sps.sources: ERCOT large-load status updates and monthly operational overview; Public Utility Commission of Texas filings
sps.verify: Definition of "approved to energise" to be fixed

sps.name: Federal rules
sps.track: FERC orders on grid operators' responses to its June 2026 large-load orders, including data centres sited at power plants.
sps.trigger: Positive if FERC approves workable rules.
sps.latest: Five of the six grid operators filed their large-load proposals by the 16 Nov deadline; Southwest Power Pool's deadline is 20 Nov. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) has not yet ruled.
sps.next: Replies to the filings due 16 Dec 2026; then a FERC ruling
sps.sources: FERC eLibrary and open-meeting agendas; Federal Register
sps.verify: The linked order sets the schedule. That the filings were made is confirmed by press reports only (Utility Dive, POWER); the docket has not been checked directly.

sps.name: Reliability outlook
sps.track: Risk ratings for PJM and ERCOT in the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Long-Term Reliability Assessment.
sps.trigger: Positive if the 2026 assessment rates 2027 to 2030 lower than the 2025 one did, and credits new supply instead of lower demand forecasts.
sps.latest: High risk from 2029
sps.sources: NERC annual and seasonal assessments; ERCOT capacity, demand and reserves report; PJM load forecast

key.label: Watch for easing
key.text: Data centres shift to regions with spare power; those sites connect on time; nuclear restarts stay on track.

calls.depends: Korea's AI Data Centre Act and Japan's Watt-Bit policy route capacity to regions with grid headroom. Nuclear restarts add firm supply for Tokyo.

sps.name: Korea's exemption threshold
sps.track: Largest data centre outside the capital region that can skip the grid impact assessment under the Act's decree.
sps.trigger: The higher the threshold, the wider the route out of Seoul. A range of 50 to 100 megawatts is under discussion.
sps.latest: Decree not yet issued
sps.next: Around the Act's entry into force, 10 Mar 2027
sps.sources: Korea National Law Information Center; Ministry of Science and ICT releases; Yonhap, Korea Herald

sps.name: Regional connections
sps.track: Number and capacity of AI data centres outside the capital region actually connected to the grid.
sps.trigger: Positive if regional sites connect in volume by 2028.
sps.latest: Baseline to be loaded with seed data
sps.sources: Korea Electric Power Corporation disclosures; Korea Power Exchange statistics; ministry designations

sps.name: Korean transmission build
sps.track: On-time delivery of 345 kilovolt lines and slippage between editions of the national electricity plan.
sps.trigger: Positive if build times shorten and fewer projects slip.
sps.latest: About nine years to build; more than half of projects delayed
sps.sources: Korea Electric Power Corporation transmission plan; Basic Plans for Electricity Supply and Demand; National Assembly audit materials

sps.name: Japanese connection times
sps.track: Quoted grid connection times for new data centres in Hokkaido, Kyushu and Osaka against Tokyo.
sps.trigger: Positive if regional times stay well below Tokyo's.
sps.latest: Osaka 3 to 5 years; Tokyo 8 to 10 years
sps.sources: Japan's grid coordination body (OCCTO); regional grid operators' capacity maps; ministry Watt-Bit materials

sps.name: Nuclear restarts
sps.track: Cumulative restarted nuclear capacity, and timing for Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Unit 7.
sps.trigger: Positive if units keep being added and Unit 7 stays on schedule.
sps.latest: 13,946 megawatts restarted, after Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Unit 6
sps.sources: Nuclear Regulation Authority; Japan Atomic Industrial Forum status sheets; International Atomic Energy Agency reactor database

key.label: Eases if
key.text: Capacity shifts to power-rich markets; connection rules ease; core-hub upgrades accelerate.

calls.depends: Grid fixes for the core hubs land after 2030: Noord-Holland 2033 to 2038, Frankfurt mid-2030s, West London 2037. Secondary markets are rationing access, and on-site gas is limited by carbon pricing.

sps.name: France and the Nordics as relief valves
sps.track: Share of new European capacity landing in France and the Nordics instead of the five core hubs; take-up of grid-ready sites; Nordic power-price spread.
sps.trigger: Positive if overflow capacity lands at scale outside the core hubs.
sps.latest: Up to 2 gigawatts of grid-ready sites in France; 3.5 gigawatts reserved in Norway
sps.sources: Broker market reports; French, Norwegian, Swedish and Finnish grid operators; European day-ahead price data

sps.name: Spain's final rules
sps.track: Whether the data centre decree is approved before the general election, and its final terms.
sps.trigger: Watch the 80% hourly renewables match, the 10 megawatt threshold and the five-year phase-in.
sps.latest: Decree awaiting Cabinet approval
sps.sources: Spain's official gazette; Council of Ministers references; energy ministry; Council of State

sps.name: Earlier grid expansions
sps.track: Whether dated grid fixes for Noord-Holland, Frankfurt and West London are brought forward or slip.
sps.trigger: Positive if any core-hub fix is brought forward to before 2030.
sps.latest: Noord-Holland 2033 to 2038; Frankfurt mid-2030s; West London 2037
sps.sources: TenneT investment plans; German grid development plan; National Grid and the UK system operator

key.label: Eases if
key.text: Project delays from local opposition fall; community benefit deals unlock approvals; state or federal rules curb local vetoes.

calls.depends: Local consent. Over half of large US projects were blocked or delayed in the second quarter of 2026. New York, Oregon and Texas have paused state permits, and an override of local vetoes looks unlikely.

sps.name: Projects disrupted
sps.track: Share, count and value of large US data centre projects blocked or delayed by local opposition.
sps.trigger: Positive if the share falls below about 25% for several consecutive quarters.
sps.latest: Over 50% disrupted; 45 projects worth US$68 billion
sps.sources: Data Center Watch quarterly reports; Ballotpedia local ballot measures; Gallup and Pew polling

gauge.label: Share of large projects blocked or delayed

sps.name: Community benefit deals
sps.track: Number and value of host-community deals, and whether they turn opposition into approvals.
sps.trigger: Positive if deals convert opposed projects into approvals.
sps.latest: New York's framework recommends at least US$1 million per megawatt invested locally
sps.sources: New York Department of Public Service; Virginia Governor's office; Loudoun and Prince William board minutes

sps.name: State or federal override
sps.track: Whether states or the federal government curb local vetoes, or tighten permitting instead.
sps.trigger: Positive if a state or federal measure limits local vetoes.
sps.latest: Loudoun County, Virginia, voted 7 to 1 on 17 Nov 2026 to pause new data centre and substation applications until as late as September 2027. This is a county tightening its own rules, not a state or federal override.
sps.next: New Congress sits Jan 2027; Oregon pause ends Jul 2027
sps.sources: Congress.gov; state bill trackers; Virginia legislative system; Federal Register
sps.verify: The linked county document is the proposal put to the vote. The result is confirmed by press reports only (Bisnow, Fox 5). The state permit pauses in New York, Oregon and Texas are not yet verified.

key.label: Stays contained if
key.text: Water rules push data centres to low-water cooling; data centres avoid water-stressed areas; southern droughts remain manageable.

calls.depends: Growth is moving into the water-scarce south. The European Union rating scheme and national rules turn water into a condition for building.

sps.name: European Union minimum standards
sps.track: Whether the proposal includes water-use limits, and at what level.
sps.trigger: Watch for limits near the 0.4 litres per kilowatt-hour benchmark, and tighter limits in water-stressed areas.
sps.latest: 2024 European Union average 0.58 litres per kilowatt-hour
sps.sources: European Commission energy directorate; EUR-Lex; public consultations

sps.name: Spain's final rules on water
sps.track: Whether the final decree keeps the top water-efficiency class for new data centres above 10 megawatts.
sps.trigger: The draft requires 0.1 litres per kilowatt-hour or less.
sps.latest: Decree awaiting Cabinet approval
sps.sources: Spain's official gazette; energy ministry; river-basin authorities

sps.name: French permit refusals
sps.track: Building permits refused for structural water stress under the law of 26 May 2026.
sps.trigger: Each refusal confirms water as a condition for building.
sps.latest: No refusals logged yet
sps.sources: Légifrance; prefectural acts; Ministry of Ecological Transition; France Datacenter

sps.name: Pipeline in water-stressed areas
sps.track: Share of new European Union data centre capacity sited in basins under high water stress.
sps.trigger: A rising share confirms the shift south.
sps.latest: Baseline to be calculated
sps.next: Improves once public labels start in Aug 2027
sps.sources: Commission data centre database; World Resources Institute Aqueduct; European Environment Agency water index

sps.name: Drought
sps.track: Share of the European Union and United Kingdom under drought warning or alert, especially Italy, Spain and Portugal.
sps.trigger: Wider or longer droughts confirm the intensification.
sps.latest: Baseline to be loaded with seed data
sps.sources: Copernicus European Drought Observatory; national hydrological bulletins

key.label: Stays contained if
key.text: Water supply keeps pace with data centre growth; data centres avoid water-stressed areas; operators shift away from water cooling.

calls.depends: Growth is concentrated in water-stressed hubs: Johor, Mumbai, Thailand's Eastern Economic Corridor and West Java. In droughts, governments put households first.

sps.name: Supply and rules keep pace
sps.track: Johor's treated-water reserve margin against its pipeline of about 8.5 gigawatts; Thailand's siting standards; whether India's hubs avoid commercial water cuts in the 2027 dry season.
sps.trigger: Positive if supply and rules keep up with the pipeline.
sps.latest: Johor reserve margin about 12.8%
sps.next: Thailand draft to the national board 27 Nov 2026
sps.sources: Malaysia's water regulator fact book; Ranhill SAJ filings; Thai reservoir data; Mumbai lake levels; India's reservoir bulletin
sps.verify: 14.4% also cited on a different basis

sps.name: Shift away from water cooling
sps.track: Share of new capacity using air-cooled or closed-loop systems; what Johor approves after its freeze; whether Thailand bars water-cooled sites from stressed areas.
sps.trigger: Positive if new approvals move to designs that use little water.
sps.latest: Johor freeze on water-cooled builds reported
sps.next: Freeze ends mid-2027 at the earliest
sps.sources: Johor state government; Malaysian Investment Development Authority; Thailand Board of Investment; Uptime Institute survey
